title: ML Fundamentals: Learning Types, Splits, Fit and Cross-Validation
summary: Revision notes on supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning, features and labels, train/validation/test splits, overfitting and underfitting, the bias-variance trade-off and cross-validation.

chapters.title: Three Learning Paradigms
points: Supervised learning: learn a mapping from inputs X to known labels y from labelled examples; regression predicts a continuous value, classification predicts a category
Unsupervised learning: find structure in unlabelled X only; clustering (k-means), dimensionality reduction (PCA), anomaly detection
Reinforcement learning: an agent acts in an environment, gets rewards, and learns a policy that maximises cumulative reward; no labelled answers, feedback is delayed
Comparison: supervised has a label per example, unsupervised has no labels, RL has a reward signal. Examples: spam filter, customer segments, game-playing agent
Interview Point: (1) Is predicting house price regression or classification? (2) How does RL differ from supervised learning? (3) Is clustering evaluated with accuracy? Why not?

chapters.title: Features, Labels and Data Splits
points: Features are the input columns X; the label (target) is the column y the model predicts; one row is one example
Train set fits the model parameters; validation set tunes hyperparameters and picks the model; test set gives one final unbiased estimate
Typical split is 60/20/20 or 70/15/15; use a stratified split for imbalanced classes and a time-ordered split for time series, never a random one
Data leakage: fitting scalers, imputers or feature selection on the full data before splitting leaks test information. Fit on train only, then transform val/test (use a Pipeline)
Interview Point: (1) Why do you need both a validation and a test set? (2) What is data leakage and how do you prevent it? (3) How do you split time-series data?

chapters.title: Overfitting and Underfitting
points: Underfitting: the model is too simple, so both train and validation error are high
Overfitting: the model memorises noise, so train error is low but validation error is much higher; the gap is the symptom
Diagnose with learning curves: error vs training size, or error vs model complexity; validation error bottoms out and then rises as complexity grows
Fix overfitting: more data, regularisation (L1/L2, dropout), simpler model, early stopping, fewer features. Fix underfitting: more capacity, better features, less regularisation, train longer
Interview Point: (1) Train accuracy 99%, test 70%: what is wrong and what do you try? (2) How does early stopping help? (3) Can more data fix underfitting?

chapters.title: Bias-Variance Trade-off
points: Expected error = bias² + variance + irreducible noise; noise cannot be removed by any model
Bias: error from wrong assumptions, so the model misses the true pattern (high bias means underfitting)
Variance: sensitivity to the particular training sample, so predictions change a lot between samples (high variance means overfitting)

More complexity lowers bias but raises variance. Linear regression is high bias and low variance, a deep decision tree is low bias and high variance. Bagging and random forests cut variance, boosting cuts bias
Interview Point: (1) Explain bias vs variance with an example. (2) Why does the trade-off exist? (3) Which ensemble method reduces variance and which reduces bias?

chapters.title: Cross-Validation in Practice
points: k-fold CV: split the data into k folds, train on k-1 and validate on 1, rotate k times, then average the scores; k=5 or 10 is the usual choice. Use cross_val_score(model, X, y, cv=5) in scikit-learn
Stratified k-fold keeps class ratios in each fold (default for classifiers); use TimeSeriesSplit for time data and GroupKFold when rows from one entity must stay together
Use CV for model selection and hyperparameter search (GridSearchCV); keep a separate untouched test set for the final score. Leave-one-out is costly and high variance
Mistakes: preprocessing outside the pipeline (leakage), tuning on the test set, reporting only the mean and ignoring the standard deviation across folds
Interview Point: (1) Why use CV instead of a single split? (2) When is plain k-fold wrong? (3) What is nested CV and why use it?

chapters.title: ML Fundamentals Cheat Sheet
points: Paradigms: supervised = X plus labels y (regression or classification), unsupervised = X only (clustering, PCA), RL = agent plus reward
Splits: train fits parameters, validation tunes, test is used once; stratify for classes, order by time for time series; fit preprocessing on train only
Diagnosis: high train and val error = underfit (high bias); low train and high val error = overfit (high variance)
Fixes: overfit means more data, regularise, simplify, early stop; underfit means more capacity, better features, less regularisation
Interview Point: (1) Walk me through your workflow from raw data to final test score. (2) How do you pick between two models? (3) Name three ways to reduce variance.
